title: Teen girl indicted on murder charges for allegedly helping spread livestream of deadly mosque shooting
summary: A North Carolina teen has been indicted for allegedly recording and spreading a deadly San Diego mosque attack livestream and manifesto.
story: Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O’Neill announced murder charges against a 17-year-old girl accused of helping record and spread a livestream of the deadly San Diego mosque shooting. (Credit: Winston-Salem Police Department / Facebook)
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide or experiencing a mental health crisis, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988.

A 17-year-old North Carolina girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting after allegedly recording a livestream of the deadly San Diego mosque shooting and sharing the attackers’ manifesto.

Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O’Neill said Monday that the teenager, identified as Sarah L. Santiago in court records, was indicted on three murder counts and one conspiracy count, according to The Associated Press.
Although she was across the country during the May 18 attack, she allegedly recorded and helped distribute the attackers’ livestream and published their manifesto.
"She disseminated that information. And she published their manifesto," O'Neill said.
NORTH CAROLINA WOMAN CHARGED IN ALLEGED HOUSTON SYNAGOGUE ATTACK PLOT AS INVESTIGATORS SEARCH FOR 2 OTHERS
People gather outside the Islamic Center of San Diego as police vehicles remain at the scene a day after a deadly shooting on May 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)
Caleb Vazquez, 18, and Cain Clark, 17, stormed the Islamic Center of San Diego armed and intending to kill people inside, according to authorities.
The gunmen killed three men — Amin Abdullah, Nadir Awad and Mansour Kaziha — who confronted them and helped prevent further bloodshed.
The attackers later died by suicide in a vehicle nearby, police said.
Authorities said the mosque was one target in a broader attack plan.

"Their plan that day was to commit mass murders not only at the mosque, but to follow up at a local Jewish temple. And finally, at a predominantly African-American high school there in town," O'Neill said.
FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES
Candles bearing the names of victims are placed outside the Islamic Center of San Diego on May 20, 2026. (Ty O'Neil/AP Photo)

The indictment alleges Santiago agreed before the attack to record and distribute the gunmen’s livestream and publish their manifesto. She is also accused of buying a patch bearing a white-supremacist symbol for one of the attackers to wear during the shooting, The Associated Press reported.
O’Neill said Santiago could face charges in North Carolina even though she was not physically present in California.

"She didn't have to be in California, she's in our jurisdiction," O'Neill said. "And today, a grand jury indicted her and held her responsible for her actions leading up to that disastrous day in May."
O’Neill noted that North Carolina law allows a 17-year-old accused of such conduct to be treated as an adult.
FBI BRINGS IRAQI MAN ACCUSED OF COORDINATING NEARLY 20 TERROR ATTACKS IN EUROPE TO FACE TRIAL IN NEW YORK
A note attached to flowers is placed outside the Islamic Center of San Diego on May 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)
Authorities said the broader investigation has included more than 100 interviews, over 30 search warrants and a review of more than 4 million messages.

"Our investigation shows that the individual had multiple opportunities to come forward to law enforcement and alert us of these deliberate actions, and the failure to do so must have consequences," FBI Charlotte Special Agent in Charge Reid Davis said.

title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty of first-degree murder in 1996 killing of Tupac Shakur
summary: Duane “Keffe D" Davis became the first person convicted in the rap icon’s 1996 drive-by shooting death after jurors deliberated for about three hours.
story: Jurors on Monday reached a verdict in the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who was charged in Tupac Shakur’s 1996 killing.
A Nevada jury on Monday found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon in the 1996 drive-by shooting death of rap icon Tupac Shakur.
Davis, 63, could face life in prison after becoming the first person convicted in the nearly 30-year-old case, according to The Associated Press.
Jurors deliberated for about three hours following closing arguments in the closely watched trial.

Shakur’s sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur, cried after the verdict was read, while Davis’ son covered his face with one hand.TUPAC MURDER TRIAL FACES ‘SNITCHES GET STITCHES’ PROBLEM BUT DEFENDANT'S GHOSTWRITER COULD BE KEY
A Nevada jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon in the 1996 drive-by shooting death of rap icon Tupac Shakur. (Raymond Boyd/Getty Images)
In closing arguments, prosecutor Binu Palal said Davis obtained a gun and "went hunting" for Shakur and Marion "Suge" Knight after they attacked Davis' nephew, according to The Associated Press.
He said Davis consistently placed himself inside the Cadillac used in the shooting.
TUPAC SHAKUR MURDER TRIAL'S FIRST WEEK HAD HEATED TESTIMONY FROM RELUCTANT WITNESSES WITH OLD GANGLAND TIES

Duane Davis stands during a break in closing arguments during his murder trial, related to the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, in Clark County District Court at the Regional Justice Center in Las Vegas, on Aug. 31, 2026. (Steve Marcus/Pool Photo via AP)
Meanwhile, defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that no evidence beyond Davis’ statements placed him in Las Vegas or inside the car.
The 16-member panel, including four alternates, heard nine days of testimony from 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses.
Davis was ordered held without bail pending sentencing, which is scheduled for Oct. 13.
TUPAC SHAKUR MURDER SUSPECT TAKES CENTER STAGE AT TRIAL NEARLY 30 YEARS AFTER SHOOTING SHOCKED MUSIC WORLD

A 1996 photo of rapper Tupac Shakur (L) and Marion "Suge" Knight is displayed during the Duane Davis murder trial, related to the 1996 killing of the rapper, at Clark County District Court at the Regional Justice Center in Las Vegas, Nevada, on Aug. 17, 2026. (STEVE MARCUS / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

A gunman in a white Cadillac opened fire on a BMW carrying Shakur and Knight on Sept. 7, 1996, on the Las Vegas Strip.  Knight recovered from minor injuries.
Shakur succumbed to his injuries six days later at 25 years old.

title: Navy unveils ‘MALICE’ missile built to strike enemy aircraft from extreme range
summary: Raytheon is developing a new 1,500-pound long-range missile, the AIM-424 LRAAM, to extend the reach and survivability of Navy and Marine aviators.
story: U.S. Central Command shared audio of Navy personnel enforcing President Donald Trump’s blockade on Iran on Monday. (Credit: @CENTCOM/X)
The U.S. Navy is developing a brand-new, extra-long-range missile designed to shoot down enemy aircraft before they can get close enough to threaten American fighter jets or aircraft carriers.
The department announced the new weapon on Aug. 22, saying the next-generation AIM-424 LRAAM is nicknamed "MALICE."
The weapon is designed to be fired from a jet to target enemy aircraft or drones at extreme distances in the air.

In practice, American pilots will be able to detect an enemy on radar, launch the missile from extreme ranges and destroy the target before coming within close proximity to the enemy, potentially increasing the pilot's survivability.
ARMY CONDUCTS FIRST OVERSEAS TEST OF 'HAMMER OF THE GODS' WEAPON-DISRUPTING SYSTEM

An AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM) is mounted in the internal weapons bay of an F-35C with an AIM-120 Advanced Medium Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM) mounted on the weapon bay door. (U.S. Navy File Photo)

"LRAAM sustains the Department’s first look, first shot, first kill advantage by providing our aviators greater reach, greater survivability, and greater tactical flexibility in the air-to-air fight," the Navy said.
The missile is designed to increase the "range, lethality, and combat effectiveness for Marine and Naval aviation forces," officials added.
EUROPE'S $116B FIGHTER JET 'FAILURE' RAISES FRESH DOUBTS ABOUT ABILITY TO DEFEND ITSELF WITHOUT US
Four AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missiles (LRAAM) are loaded on an F/A-18E Super Hornet for a test event. (U.S. Navy File Photo)

Its range is listed as "in excess" of 250 nautical miles, or roughly 287 statute miles. That is a massive distance for an air-to-air missile, allowing jets to protect an entire fleet from far over the horizon.

At 13.5 feet long and weighing 1,500 pounds, the missile is significantly larger and heavier than standard medium-range air-to-air missiles. In comparison, the AIM-120 AMRAAM weighs about 335 pounds, underscoring the size of the propulsion system needed to propel the LRAAM to extreme distances.

FILE — Two F/A-18 Super Hornets launch from the flight deck of the U.S. Navy Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln. Officials recently tested the new AIM-424 LRAAM missile on F/A-18 Super Hornets. (U.S. Navy/Handout via Reuters)

The missile is also equipped with a blast-fragmentation warhead, meaning it does not necessarily have to score a direct physical hit. Instead, it detonates near the target, sending fragments outward to destroy or disable the aircraft.
Officials said the missile is compatible with aircraft across multiple generations, including fourth and fifth-generation fighters as well as future sixth-generation aircraft.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The LRAAM is being developed by Raytheon, one of the U.S. military’s primary defense contractors.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Knife-wielding woman accused of stabbing 2 in Times Square before being shot by police
summary: A knife-wielding woman allegedly stabbed two people in Times Square Monday before advancing on NYPD officers, who deployed a Taser and then opened fire.
story: Fox News' Todd Piro provides details on an incident in Times Square after a woman armed with kitchen knives stabbed two people, killing one. NYPD officers reportedly deployed tasers before shooting the suspect.
A woman armed with two knives went on a random stabbing spree through the heart of Times Square Monday before a tense confrontation with NYPD officers ended in deadly gunfire, authorities said.

The attack left a 32-year-old woman dead and a 68-year-old man wounded after the two strangers were stabbed within just 20 seconds of each other, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said during an evening news conference.
Police identified the alleged attacker as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros of Queens, who was also killed after officers opened fire.
The violence began around 4:24 p.m. near West 41st Street and Seventh Avenue, where a 68-year-old man had just exited the subway and was standing with his wife waiting to cross the street.
WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS
Large police presence currently in Times Square. (Fox 5)

A witness told investigators Cisneros pulled two knives from a red Target bag, waved them and approached the man before stabbing him in the right side of his abdomen in what Tisch called a "random and unprovoked attack."
The man was rushed to Bellevue Hospital and remained in stable condition Monday evening.
Cisneros then headed north on Seventh Avenue toward West 42nd Street, where police said she approached a 32-year-old woman and stabbed her in the abdomen in another apparently random attack.
MAN DEAD, ANOTHER CRITICAL AFTER DOUBLE STABBING AT BROOKLYN PARK AS POLICE DETAIN PERSON OF INTEREST: NYPD
The NYPD have confirmed that there was a police-involved shooting in Times Square. (Fox 5)
The woman was rushed to Bellevue, where she died from her injuries. Police had not released her identity pending notification of her family.
The two attacks unfolded within approximately 20 seconds of each other, Tisch said. The second stabbing was captured on an NYPD Argus camera.
NYPD OFFICERS FATALLY SHOOT MAN ARMED WITH BUTCHER KNIFE AFTER HE ADVANCED TOWARD COPS: POLICE
As Cisneros continued north, witnesses flagged down officers who confronted her between West 42nd and West 43rd streets. She was still holding both knives, police said.
What followed was a roughly four-minute standoff as officers repeatedly ordered Cisneros to drop the weapons and attempted to talk her into surrendering them.
MACHETE-WIELDING SUSPECT CLAIMING TO BE 'LUCIFER' SHOT BY POLICE AFTER ALLEGEDLY STABBING 3 AT TRANSIT HUB

The two knives NYPD said were recovered after Pamela Cisneros allegedly stabbed two strangers in an unprovoked Times Square attack that left a 32-year-old woman dead and a 68-year-old man wounded. (X/@NYPDnews)
But she made clear she had no intention of surrendering the knives, Tisch said.
"I’m not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you," Cisneros told the officers, according to Tisch.
"I will kill you," she repeated.
Police said Cisneros then began waving the knives and advancing toward the officers. Multiple officers deployed Tasers, but they failed to stop her.
As Cisneros continued advancing with the knives, two officers opened fire, striking her. She was taken to Bellevue Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.
The confrontation and police shooting were captured on officers’ body-worn cameras, Tisch said.
EIGHT NYPD OFFICERS INJURED IN MASSIVE EXPLOSION WHILE RESPONDING TO KNIFE-WIELDING MAN IN QUEENS HOME

NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch speaks at a press conference alongside New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and police officials following the deadly double stabbing and police-involved shooting in Times Square on Aug. 31, 2026. (X/@NYPDnews)
"This was an extraordinarily dangerous situation unfolding in the heart of Times Square, the crossroads of the world," Tisch said.
She noted that thousands of New Yorkers, commuters, tourists, families and workers can be moving through the area at any given moment.
"Our officers were confronted with a rapidly evolving threat, with countless innocent people around them," Tisch said. "In that moment, they did what we train them to do."
Mayor Zohran Mamdani also credited the responding officers with preventing further bloodshed.
NYPD OFFICER SHOT, GUNMAN KILLED AFTER ARMED BARRICADED STANDOFF IN BROOKLYN: POLICE
The NYPD have confirmed on X that there is currently an investigation near West 42nd Street and 7th Avenue. (Fox 5)

"I want to thank the NYPD officers who stepped in and prevented a horrific attack from becoming even worse," Mamdani said. "This is what the men and women of this department do every single day to keep our city safe."
Mamdani said the standard internal investigation into the police shooting will take place and that body-worn camera footage will be released to the public.

Cisneros had no arrest history with the NYPD, but department records documented a mental health history involving police interactions in 2018 and 2019, Tisch said. Investigators were still working to determine what brought her to Times Square before the attack.
Police said there was no reason at this stage of the investigation to believe the stabbing was an act of terrorism.
Tisch called the killing a "senseless act of violence" as she reflected on the victim and the family now confronting her death.

"One life cut far too short by a senseless act of violence," Tisch said. "There are family members and loved ones who are now confronting the unimaginable loss, and our hearts are with them."

title: Bryan Kohberger's new lawyer says key questions may soon get answers in court
summary: Bryan Kohberger's new lawyer says upcoming filings will address unanswered questions about the Idaho student murders guilty plea withdrawal.
story: Legal maneuvers escalate in the Idaho student murders case as Bryan Kohberger attempts to disqualify Judge Steven Hippler. Fox News legal analyst Gregg Jarrett breaks down the defense's strategy.

Bryan Kohberger's newest lawyer says upcoming filings and a potential evidentiary hearing will shed new light on the Idaho student murders case while their immediate legal fight concerns the constitutionality of the plea his client is attempting to withdraw.

"We think the [amended] PCR and evidentiary hearing will naturally address some of the outstanding and unanswered questions," Jason Goldman, a New York-based attorney who is joining Kohberger's team, told Fox News Digital Monday. "That said, the main priority right now is to scrutinize the constitutional issues surrounding Bryan's plea."

Kohberger, in a handwritten petition for post-conviction relief filed in July, told the court he had ineffective counsel, that his guilty plea was "not knowingly or voluntarily entered because it was induced by unkept promises" and that it was "not voluntarily entered because of threats asserted by petitioner's (Kohberger's) legal counsel."
BRYAN KOHBERGER'S POST-CONVICTION RELIEF BID ENABLED BY FLAWED PLEA DEAL, PSYCHOLOGIST ARGUES

University of Idaho students Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Xana Kernodle and Ethan Chapin were killed in a November 2022 attack at an off-campus house on King Road in Moscow, Idaho. (Idaho Statesman/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"The circumstances surrounding Bryan's plea — and what occurred in the critical days leading up to it — deserve careful, independent judicial scrutiny," Goldman said. "Some of those circumstances are already part of the public record. Others are not."
He also said that the support Kohberger receives from his family is part of why he agreed to join the case.
BRYAN KOHBERGER'S MOTHER CALLED HIM 'MY ANGEL' AND INSISTED POLICE MADE A 'REALLY, REALLY BAD MISTAKE': BOOK

Bryan Kohberger appears at the Ada County Courthouse for his sentencing hearing on July 23, 2025, in Boise, Idaho. Kohberger pleaded guilty in exchange for being spared the death penalty for the stabbing of four University of Idaho students nearly three years ago. (Kyle Green-Pool/Getty Images)
"Most family and friends run for the hills when a loved one is quietly arrested, let alone charged with a highly-publicized murder," he said. "The unwavering support Bryan maintains speaks volumes."

Judge Steven Hippler set a Nov. 13 deadline for Kohberger's lawyers to file an amended petition which is expected to be written by attorneys and include more in-depth legal arguments than the handwritten petition Kohberger submitted in July.
BRYAN KOHBERGER’S 2027 HEARING IS NOT GUARANTEED AS IDAHO SEEKS QUICK DISMISSAL
Idaho defense attorney Greg Rauch was appointed to represent Kohberger last month. Goldman said he would be joining as out-of-state counsel but is not yet officially on the docket.

Bryan Kohberger arrives at a Pennsylvania courthouse for an extradition hearing in January 2023. He pleaded guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students on July 1, 2025. (The Image Direct for Fox News Digital)

Prosecutors have asked the judge to dismiss Kohberger's petition on numerous grounds, but Kohberger's lawyers filed a motion last week to have the judge removed from the case and to change the venue back to Moscow, Idaho, where the offices of Rauch and the Latah County Prosecuting Attorney are both located.
Kohberger had previously sought a change of venue out of Latah County, where the murders took place, which landed him in front of Hippler in Ada County.

title: US Fish and Wildlife Service officer dies during wildfire evacuation efforts in Oklahoma, agency says
summary: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service officer David Taylor was going door-to-door to evacuate Oklahoma families when he made his last contact with dispatch.
story: Fox News correspondent Max Gorden has the latest on the wildfire on Fox News.
A federal wildlife officer is believed to have died while helping evacuate residents threatened by a wildfire in Oklahoma, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service said over the weekend.

Officials said David Taylor, 38, of Scio, Oregon, was helping people fleeing the fast-moving fire south of Oklahoma City on Saturday. He was going door-to-door to help residents alongside emergency crews.
His last contact with dispatch came while he was assisting a family in leaving their home, the agency said.
11 NATIONAL PARK SERVICE WORKERS EVACUATED BY HELICOPTER AMID CALIFORNIA FIRE

U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service federal wildlife officer David Taylor, 38, is believed to have died while helping evacuate residents from their homes over the weekend during the Railroad South Fire in Oklahoma, the agency said. (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service)

"Everything we know about David's actions demonstrates extraordinary courage and selflessness," said U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik. " When people were in danger, David was there helping them get to safety. He remained committed to protecting others under the most dangerous circumstances. We mourn alongside his family, friends and colleagues, and we will never forget his service."
Evidence recovered from a structure led officials to believe Taylor died during the evacuation effort, authorities said.
MARINE VETERAN AND BOSTON FIREFIGHTER DIES AFTER RESCUE EFFORTS AT MASSIVE HOUSE BLAZE

At the time of his death, Taylor was a senior chief petty officer in the Navy Reserve and previously served on active duty. During his 20 years of naval service, Taylor completed five deployments, including one to Iraq and four to Djibouti.

Taylor also served the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service at the Rio Mora National Wildlife Refuge and the Las Vegas National Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico before joining the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in Oklahoma.
The Fish and Wildlife Service and the Department of the Interior were coordinating support for Taylor’s family and co-workers, the agency said.

Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt has ordered all American and Oklahoma flags on state property to be flown at half-staff Sept. 1 through Sept. 4 in honor of Taylor.

"Sarah and I are praying for his family, his fellow officers and everyone who was impacted by this tragedy," he wrote on X. "His courage, selflessness and devotion to protecting others will never be forgotten."
The Railroad South Fire in Comanche County, Oklahoma, was reported on Saturday. All evacuation orders for residents affected by the wildfire have been lifted.

title: FBI extradites former Ten Most Wanted fugitive arrested for 2000 murder of 5-year-old girl in Philadelphia
summary: Alexis Flores, wanted for the alleged rape and murder of 5-year-old Iriana DeJesus in Philadelphia, was extradited from Honduras after 25 years.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
The FBI secured the extradition of a Honduran national wanted for over 25 years for the alleged rape and murder of a 5-year-old girl in Philadelphia on Monday.

Alexis Flores was arrested in Honduras in February and connected to the alleged 2000 rape and murder of 5-year-old Iriana DeJesus, FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. The FBI listed Flores on its top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list, and authorities in Honduras agreed to extradite him to U.S. custody.

"Alexis Flores is yet another high value target brought back by this FBI, after he was arrested in Honduras in February by an anti-gang transnational task force connected to the 2000 murder of a 5-year-old girl, Iriana DeJesus," Patel told Fox News Digital. "After more than 25 years on the run, this arrest proves time and distance do not shield violent offenders from justice."
EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS

Alexis Flores was previously a top 10 FBI fugitive, according to officials. He was arrested Wednesday in Honduras in connection with the 2000 murder of a young girl in Philadelphia. (FBI and Google Maps)

"This also comes as the FBI and Trump administration continue an unprecedented run of man hunting violent fugitives. This FBI has conducted nearly over 70 similar extraditions since the start of June. More than ever before, violent criminals cannot hide from the reach of law enforcement. Thank you to our overseas partners, department of justice, and brilliant FBI teams who got this done," Patel said.
The FBI said Flores had been removed from the fugitives list in March 2025 due to the prior Honduran government’s refusal to extradite him for his offenses, citing local laws limiting extradition.
PATEL SAYS FBI IS 'MANHUNTING' TERROR SUSPECTS AROUND THE GLOBE AFTER TWO HIGH-VALUE CAPTURES
Alexis Flores was a top 10 FBI fugitive, according to officials. (FBI)
Authorities in Philadelphia celebrated Flores' arrest when authorities apprehended him in Honduras earlier this year.

"The passage of time does not diminish our resolve or perseverance in the pursuit of justice," said Wayne Jacobs, special agent in charge of FBI Philadelphia, in February. "The arrest of Alexis Flores is the culmination of 25 years of tireless investigative effort and the strength of our partnerships across departments. Through this sustained collaboration and the support of our law enforcement partners, both domestically and internationally, the day is now here."
COLD-CASE FUGITIVE BUSTED SOUTH OF THE BORDER AS NEW DNA TECH ALLEGEDLY TIES HIM TO TEEN’S ROADSIDE KILLING

Flores' extradition comes just weeks after the FBI captured Most Wanted fugitive Gregory Henderson Jr., just three days after adding the alleged Indianapolis gang leader to its list and offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.

FBI Director Kash Patel speaks during a press conference on October 23, 2025 in New York City. He announced indictments against current and former N.B.A. players in a pair of criminal cases that involved the coordination of Mafia families and professional athletes. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Henderson, 46, had evaded arrest since a sweeping federal takedown of his alleged organization in August 2023. He faces federal charges of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute and to distribute controlled substances, conspiracy to launder monetary instruments and conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture.

The FBI alleges Henderson led a violent Indianapolis gang whose drug trafficking network was supplied by the Sinaloa Cartel and distributed methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl throughout Indianapolis and the surrounding Midwest.

title: Colorado family wakes up to bear eating breakfast in kitchen
summary: Security footage captures a bear raiding a Colorado Springs kitchen, eating Flintstones vitamins and trash before an 8-year-old helped scare it off.
story: A Colorado family wakes up to an unexpected breakfast guest after a bear strolls through their open back door and helps itself in the kitchen.
A Colorado family woke up one July and found a bear making itself at home and eating breakfast in their kitchen.
Security camera footage from inside the Colorado Springs home shows the bear entering the kitchen on July 21 and grabbing a snack.
"I was getting ready in the morning and heard a bang. I asked my kids — 8, 6 and 3 years old — if they were all okay, and they were all upstairs playing," Nerissa England told Storyful.
GATLINBURG POLICE FREE BLACK BEAR THAT LOCKED ITSELF INSIDE HOTEL BATHROOM IN WILD VIRAL VIDEO
A bear entered the home of a Colorado family and ate the food on a kitchen table before taking a trash can outside. (Storyful)

"I assumed it was a picture that had fallen off the wall, so my curious 8-year-old daughter, Zara Lee, went downstairs to investigate, and my husband followed to grab coffee," England added. "She rounded the corner into our kitchen, and a bear was eating our trash right outside the kitchen door."
The bear apparently walked into the home through a back door that was left open so that a breeze could come in amid the hot temperatures.
COLORADO BLACK BEAR DIES AFTER BECOMING TRAPPED INSIDE UNLOCKED CAR FOR DAYS: REPORT
A black bear in a grassy area. (Getty Images Creatives)
The animal then ate some Flintstones vitamins left on a table, dragged a trash can outside and began rummaging through it near the kitchen door, England said.
Zara Lee and her father reportedly managed to scare the bear away by opening the door and making noise.
CALIFORNIA COUPLE FIGHTS OFF 70-POUND BLACK BEAR WITH HATCHET AND WATER BOTTLE OUTSIDE THEIR HOME
"We will be keeping the door shut for a while until the local bears get the food they need and go into hibernation!" England told Storyful.
Black bear on road at Mount Rainier, Wash. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)
Bears have wandered into people's homes across the United States in record numbers after a dry winter wiped out plants, grasses, berries and nuts that form around 90% of their diet, Reuters reported.

Their sense of smell has lured them to places with human food. This has led to record bear deaths in some states, as hundreds have been euthanized, run over, shot and even electrocuted as they interact with humans.

title: Texas fire department makes save on crane 22 stories in the air
summary: The Fort Worth Fire Department shared photos and detailed the rescue of an individual from the cab of a towering crane in the Lone Star State.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Responders rescued an individual from the cab of a towering crane in Texas on Saturday, according to the Fort Worth Fire Department.
The department detailed the save in a Saturday Facebook post, which noted that the individual was about 220 feet high.

"The Fort Worth Fire Department Alarm Office received a call for a medical emergency at 11:50am today," the post noted, explaining, "The location was at... the construction site at JPS Health Hospital. Upon arrival, crews found that the patient was actually located approximately 220 feet up in the air, inside of a crane cab."
The Fort Worth Fire Department shared photos in a Facebook post that described a rescue operation to lower an individual from a towering crane. (Facebook/Fort Worth Fire Department)
Responders climbed up, provided medical aid and lowered the individual to the ground, the department noted.

"When technical rescue teams arrived on scene, they gathered gear and began their ascent up the crane’s ladder. They carried with them all of the equipment they would need for the entire rescue on their backs," the department said.
The Fort Worth Fire Department shared photos in a Facebook post that described a rescue operation to lower an individual from a towering crane. (Facebook/Fort Worth Fire Department)

"Upon arrival at the top of the crane (over 22 stories in the air), they went to work. Immediate emergency medical care was started while technical rescue teams began devising a plan for the patient’s safe descent," the department continued.

"Once the patient was safely hooked up to the ropes and rigging system, the crews had him lowered and on the ground. This all happened within less than an hour of their making it to him initially," the post read.
The department shared multiple photos of the heroic rescue effort.
The Fort Worth Fire Department shared photos in a Facebook post that described a rescue operation to lower an individual from a towering crane. (Facebook/Fort Worth Fire Department)

"The crane operator was then transported to the hospital in stable condition," the department added.
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Illinois man missing more than a week as crews scour Great Smoky Mountains National Park
summary: A 57-member team is using drones to search Great Smoky Mountains National Park for Marcin Bachleda-Blaszczak after his car was found at a visitor center.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A 57-member search team is combing Great Smoky Mountains National Park for an Illinois man who has been missing for more than a week after his vehicle was found at a popular visitor center.

Marcin Bachleda-Blaszczak was last known to be at the Sugarlands Visitor Center parking lot on August 22, 2025, according to the National Park Service (NPS). He was reported missing two days later and his vehicle was then found in the visitor center’s parking lot.

Park rangers and volunteers, along with local agencies, have expanded the search in and around the park, looking both on and off trails and using drones to help cover the area, as they look for Bachleda-Blaszczak, according to NPS.
73-YEAR-OLD CAMPER VANISHES OFF THE GRID BEFORE HIS RV TURNS UP IN WILDERNESS
Marcin Bachleda-Blaszczak was last known to be at the Sugarlands Visitor Center parking lot on Aug. 22, according to the National Park Service (NPS). (National Park Service)
Drones are normally prohibited inside Great Smoky Mountains National Park, which straddles the border between North Carolina and Tennessee, but are temporarily being allowed for the search.
Bachleda-Blaszczak's family said nothing seemed unusual shortly before he disappeared.
Bachleda-Blaszczak is described as 5 feet, 6 inches tall and approximately 170 pounds, with brown hair and blue eyes. (National Park Service)
"The day before, I believe, was when he had pizza with his dad, you know, chatted with him, said he might pick up a shift the next day at work," his cousin, Corrina Auten, told CBS Chicago.
"It was very, you know, like a normal, normal conversation. There wasn't anything strange or amiss," she said. "The next thing we knew, he didn't show up for work and he was missing."

Foot bridge across the creek along the Fighting Creek Nature Trail originating at the Sugarland Visitors Center on the Tennessee side of the Great Smoky Mountains National Park. (Ron Buskirk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)
URGENT SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR MORE THAN A DOZEN PEOPLE AFTER GRAND CANYON FLASH FLOOD
Rangers first searched the area around Sugarlands before widening their search. The team grew to 47 rangers and volunteers by Saturday and 57 by Sunday, according to the NPS.
Bachleda-Blaszczak is described as 5 feet, 6 inches tall and approximately 170 pounds, with brown hair and blue eyes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Officials asked anyone with information or who believes they have seen Bachleda-Blaszczak to contact Great Smoky Mountains National Park dispatch at GRSM_Dispatch@nps.gov.

title: South Carolina woman accused of stabbing Lyft driver 11 times claims mental health crisis
summary: A South Carolina woman's attorney says schizophrenia and paranoia triggered a psychiatric emergency before she allegedly stabbed her Lyft driver 11 times.
story: Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, R-Ga., emphasizes the urgent need for enhanced law enforcement presence on public transit and around stations following the stabbing of a 66-year-old woman.

A South Carolina woman accused of stabbing her Lyft driver 11 times before taking his vehicle was denied bond Friday as her attorney argued she was experiencing a severe mental health crisis during the alleged attack.

Naziyha Weatherall faces charges of attempted murder, carjacking and possession of a weapon during a violent crime in Greenville County. The charges stem from an April 22 incident, court records show.
FOX Carolina reported that prosecutors called the allegations a "frightening factual scenario" during Friday’s bond hearing and argued Weatherall posed an extreme danger to the community.
FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED IN IHOP RESTAURANT AFTER POLICE SAY HE STABBED A RIDESHARE DRIVER

"The victim was simply just trying to do his job and was stabbed 11 times," a solicitor said, according to FOX Carolina. "Not only was he stabbed 11 times, his car was then carjacked by this defendant."
Naziyha Weatherall faces charges of attempted murder, carjacking and possession of a weapon during a violent crime in Greenville County. (Greenville County Sheriff's Office)
The driver’s wife appeared in court on his behalf, saying the trauma of the alleged attack prevented him from attending.

"What concerns us most is that happened while my husband was simply working," she said. "He was not looking for any confrontation, he was providing a service to a person. If this level of violence could happen to someone who was simply doing his job, we are concerned about potential risks to other people in our community."
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Weatherall’s lawyer urged the court to view the allegations through the lens of her mental state, saying she had never previously been charged with a crime and was in the throes of a psychiatric emergency.
CHARLOTTE TRAIN STABBING SUSPECT DODGES POTENTIAL DEATH PENALTY FOR NOW AFTER HE'S RULED INCOMPETENT

Naziyha Weatherall faces charges of attempted murder, carjacking and possession of a weapon during a violent crime in Greenville County, in which she is accused of stabbing a Lyft driver 11 times. (iStock)
The defense said paranoia had convinced Weatherall that others were monitoring her and trying to harm her, prompting her to summon a ride to report her fears to police.

"Her mother even called the police station to let them know she was on the way to make a report," the attorney said. "During that, the crisis got worse."

The attorney said Weatherall believed she was being trafficked, panicked during the ride and had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and other mental health conditions.
Greenville, South Carolina, is pictured beside a booking photo of Naziyha Weatherall. (Getty ; Greenville County Sheriff's Office)

The defense said Weatherall is now medicated, stable and competent, and asked the court to release her so relatives and a social worker could arrange placement at a treatment facility.
BOYFRIEND ACCUSED OF STABBING DEFENSE TECH ENGINEER 15 TIMES DENIED BOND AFTER 911 CALL PLAYED IN COURT
Weatherall’s mother apologized to the driver’s family while asking the court to consider her daughter’s mental state.

title: Newark airport shuttle bus slams into concrete barrier, injuring 13
summary: Video shows the badly damaged employee shuttle bus crumpled against a concrete barrier at Newark Liberty International Airport's Terminal B.
story: An employee shuttle bus crashed into a concrete barrier at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey early Monday, injuring 13 people. (Credit: FNTV)
An employee shuttle bus crashed into a concrete barrier at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey early Monday, injuring 13 people, according to local reports.
The crash happened shortly after 3 a.m. on the Terminal B Departures Level 3 roadway, News 12 New Jersey reported.
Three people suffered serious injuries, while 10 others sustained minor injuries, according to the report. None of the injuries were believed to be life-threatening.
BUS CRASH NEAR PENTAGON INJURES 23, INCLUDING 10 WAR DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL
Three people suffered serious injuries, while 10 others sustained minor injuries, according to local reports. None of the injuries were believed to be life-threatening. (FreedomNewsTV (FNTV))

Video obtained by Fox News Digital showed the badly damaged shuttle bus still pressed against the concrete barrier in the aftermath of the crash. The front end appeared crumpled, while glass from the bus door and windshield were shattered.
Police tape surrounded the crash site as first responders worked nearby.
It was unclear what caused the crash. Authorities are continuing to investigate. (FreedomNewsTV (FNTV))
The injured were transported to area hospitals for evaluation and treatment, according to WABC-TV.
The crash prompted authorities to close the Terminal B Departures Level 3 roadway as crews worked to clear debris from the area.
The crash happened shortly after 3 a.m. on the Terminal B Departures Level 3 roadway, prompting authorities to close the roadway as debris was cleared. (FreedomNewsTV (FNTV))
LAGUARDIA SHUTS DOWN RUNWAY FOR SECOND TIME IN WEEKS AFTER PAVEMENT ISSUE RESURFACES
The Port Authority Police Department advised passengers departing from Terminal B to be dropped off on Level 2 because of the police activity.
Authorities have not released the cause of the crash.

The investigation is ongoing.

title: Deadly Grand Canyon flooding knocks out critical water line amid race to find missing hikers
summary: A 46-year-old man was found dead and one other body was recovered in the Colorado River as search and rescue teams race to locate over a dozen missing hikers in the Grand Canyon area.
story: Footage from the Grand Canyon this weekend shows rescue workers airlifting a group of hikers out of the Grand Canyon after flash flooding caused "extensive" damage on Saturday.

Severe flash flooding knocked out a central water line in the Grand Canyon this weekend, forcing the National Park Service to implement strict water restrictions amid an ongoing race to find missing hikers.

NPS says it will implement stage four water restrictions beginning at 12:00 p.m. on Monday, saying the Saturday flooding caused "extensive damage to infrastructure," including the Transcanyon Waterline that supplies the park with water. Park officials say 2 people were killed and 15 may be missing after the flooding, though they say that is an estimate.

Park officials confirmed they recovered the body of a 46-year-old man from the Colorado River on Sunday night. He has not been publicly identified. Authorities recovered a second body on Monday, but they have not released further details.
MISSING GRAND CANYON HIKER, 83, RESCUED AFTER GETTING SEPARATED FROM COMPANION
Bright Angel Creek near the Phantom Ranger Station in the Grand Canyon, Arizona, is seen after flash flooding from storms, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (Parth Desai via AP)
NPS issued a request for the public to provide information on the 15 other people who are believed to be missing.

"The National Park Service is asking anyone who knows of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on August 29, as well as anyone who had a campground reservation in the affected corridor, to provide information to the National Park Service Investigative Services Branch," NPS said in a statement.
AMERICAN HIKER VANISHES ON TROPICAL TREK AS FLASH FLOODS, MUDSLIDES TURN JUNGLE GETAWAY INTO DESPERATE SEARCH

This photo provided by the National Park Service shows remnants of stone bridge pylons along Bright Angel Creek in the Grand Canyon following a flash flood that destroyed the footbridge, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (James Thompson/National Park Service via AP)
Park officials say they have so far evacuated at least 62 people since the Saturday flooding.

The stage 4 water restrictions affecting the rest of the park include forced dry camping with no access to water spigots, the temporary closure of overnight lodgings, and a strict no-fire rule for the South Rim and inner canyon areas.
ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES
The flooding struck Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Aug. 29, according to NPS, which added that nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed.
Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs said state emergency officials are coordinating with federal and local authorities as the search continues.
EXPERTS ZERO IN ON LIKELY CAUSE OF DEADLY NEPAL MUDSLIDE, WITH MORE THAN 1,400 MISSING

"My heart is with the families and loved ones of every person unaccounted for after the flash flooding at the Grand Canyon," Hobbs wrote on X. "DEMA is coordinating with NPS and Coconino County Emergency Management to support search and recovery efforts."
Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs released a statement following flash flooding in the Grand Canyon this weekend. (Rebecca Noble/Getty Images)

Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes called the flash flooding "devastating" and thanked first responders for searching for those still unaccounted for and evacuating others from the affected area.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The physical damage includes a historic lodge near the bottom of the site and untold environmental upheaval," Fontes said in a statement. "I send my prayers to the community as the search for those unaccounted for continues."
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.
